ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all officers, directors, shareholders, and every 10%+ beneficial owner against: (i) OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List and Consolidated Non-SDN List; (ii) UN Security Council Consolidated List; (iii) Government of Canada consolidated SEMA and SPA autonomous sanctions regulations and Canadian Consolidated Autonomous Sanctions List; (iv) United Kingdom consolidated list; and (v) EU CFSP list. Enhanced due diligence is required for politically exposed persons (PEPs), including Canadian provincial and federal domestic PEPs, using the FINTRAC definition of domestic vs. foreign PEP; on an enhanced basis for social-casino payment volume, additional screening against BC Gaming Policy Enforcement Branch and FINTRAC Money Service Business indicators shall be documented even where the entity is not a licensed casino. The AML risk tier is Medium_Risk_Enhanced; all KYC and screening results must be maintained for at least five years after the business relationship terminates.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: BC Registry Services (formerly OneStop Corporate Registry) at https://www.bcregistryservices.gov.bc.ca/ and federal NUANS search for corporate name clearance
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names in British Columbia must be expressed in English or French using Latin-alphabet characters and accepted numerals and symbols. Non-Latin scripts such as Cyrillic, Arabic, or CJK ideographs are not accepted in the registered corporate name; mandatory transliteration into a Latin-script English or French form must be provided. The name must not contain a sign, character, or mark that is not commonly used in English or French. Accented letters in French are permitted. Corporate designations for ULCs must be in an accepted form, generally 'Unlimited Liability Company' or 'ULC'. The name is distinguishable only if it does not conflict with existing BC and federal trademark/corporate registers under the BCBCA Name Regulations.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon receipt of a name reservation rejection notice from the BC Registrar, the applicant may file a Request for Reconsideration or substitute name request through BC Registry Services within 30 days of the rejection date. The submission must address the registrar's stated conflict, offending prohibited token, or misleading/confusing similarity, and must provide a side-by-side comparison, acceptable distinguishing elements, and, where applicable, evidence of consent from the holder of a conflicting name or trademark. If the registrar affirms the rejection, the applicant may file a judicial review application in the Supreme Court of British Columbia under the Business Corporations Act and the judicial review procedure act; the application must be filed promptly after the decision, with supporting legal argument and any material harm from the refusal. A simultaneous NEW name reservation request is advisable to preserve the 56-day clearance window.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A registered office in British Columbia must be an actual physical street address in BC, not a postal box only; however, a commercial virtual office provider that offers a dedicated BC street address, mail acceptance, and statutory process service during business hours is generally permissible for the registered office. For an active software-publishing ULC, the virtual office must be supported by a physical operating location, call handling procedure, and records-management facility sufficient to satisfy directors' due diligence, FINTRAC CDD expectations, and BC corporate records inspection requirements. The use of a bare virtual office will be insufficient if the corporation cannot demonstrate a corporate substance or record-retention at the address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 15% probability of an unannounced physical on-site inspection within the first operational year for a non-licensed social-casino software publisher; the probability rises to 35-40% if the company later engages in real-money, sweepstakes, or geoblocked interactive-gaming activities involving BC residents, or if FINTRAC/MSB thresholds are crossed through high-volume virtual-currency or app-payment settlements.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act, SBC 2002, c. 57 (BCBCA): s. 2 (definition of unlimited liability company), ss. 51-54 (incorporation and certificate of incorporation), s. 96 (registered office), ss. 121-127 (directors), ss. 128-133 (special rules for unlimited liability companies); supplemented by Business Corporations Regulation, SBC 2002, c. 57 reg. 1 and applicable CRA rulings on ULC tax treatment.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: BC Registrar of Companies, Corporate Registry, Ministry of Finance, Province of British Columbia, operating through the BC Corporate Online and OneStop Business Registry electronic filing systems.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation Application (Form 1) and Notice of Articles (Form 10) filed electronically under the BCBCA; Certificate of Incorporation (Form 2) issued by the Registrar upon approval.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; the BCBCA permits incorporation with nil or nominal share consideration, and no escrow, bank deposit, or capital funding condition is imposed. The unlimited liability attribute affects shareholder exposure to creditor claims, not pre-funding requirements.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT the Incorporators' share subscriptions are hereby approved, and the Corporation issues one Class A Common Voting Share to the subscriber named in the Subscription Agreement, credited as fully paid for nominal consideration. RESOLVED THAT the registered office of the Corporation is established at the address stated in the Notice of Articles in Vancouver, British Columbia, and the Notice of Articles is affirmed. RESOLVED THAT the directors named in the incorporation application are elected, and the following officers are appointed: Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer, and Corporate Secretary, to hold office until successors are elected. RESOLVED THAT the Corporate Secretary is authorized to open bank accounts, register the Corporation with the Canada Revenue Agency, and execute ancillary filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registry Services – Corporate Name Request module of BC Corporate Online (OneStop Business Registry)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an online Name Request for up to three proposed corporate names ending in 'Unlimited Liability Company' or 'ULC'. The registry performs a NUANS search of federal and provincial corporate names and trademarks. Upon approval, the name reservation is valid for 56 calendar days and is renewable once for an additional 56 days.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name and two alternate names
Email address and contact details of the incorporator or authorized agent
Name Request filing fee payment
Description of the Corporation's proposed business activity (ISIC 5820 / NAICS 511210)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Name Request is rejected due to a conflict, prohibited word, or mark, file a revised Name Request with distinctive geographical or descriptive elements, or obtain and upload the written consent of the conflicting name holder; resubmit through the same BC Corporate Online portal without needing a new account.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Incorporation Application and Notice of Articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registrar of Companies, Corporate Registry – BC Corporate Online / OneStop electronic filing system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the online Incorporation Application (Form 1) and Notice of Articles (Form 10), electing the entity as an Unlimited Liability Company, designating the registered office address, appointing at least one director ordinarily resident in Canada or as permitted by the BCBCA for ULCs, and setting the authorized share structure with one class of common voting shares. Pay the CA$350 filing fee by credit card and submit; the Certificate of Incorporation and incorporation number are issued electronically upon approval.
required_dossiers: Incorporation Application (Form 1)
Notice of Articles (Form 10)
Director consent forms (Form 3) for each director
Registered office address and mailing address within British Columbia
Authorized share structure and share class summary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a requisition letter or notice of defect, file a corrective response within the specified period (typically 14 days) through BC Corporate Online, submitting amended Form 1 or a Notice of Articles amendment; late corrections attract supplementary fees and may require re-instatement of the name reservation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Initial Share Issuance and Statutory Corporate Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered agent and corporate records office of the Corporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the Certificate of Incorporation is issued, prepare and issue the share certificate for the subscribed Class A common shares, formalize the unanimous shareholder agreement if intended, organize the corporate minute book containing the incorporation documents, and record the first board resolutions. The records must be kept at the registered office and made available for inspection in accordance with the BCBCA record-keeping provisions.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Notice of Articles
Shareholder subscription agreement
Minute book, share certificate stubs, and transfer register
Director consent and officer appointment forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a share certificate or minute book record shows a clerical defect, cancel and re-issue the affected certificate, have the secretary certify the correction by resolution, and replace the defective document in the records office; no filing with the Registrar is required unless the Notice of Articles is affected.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with Canada Revenue Agency for Business Number and Tax Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) – Business Registration Online (BRO), including provincial linkages through OneStop
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the issued incorporation number, register with CRA to obtain the 9-digit Business Number (BN) and activate required program accounts: GST/HST (RC0001) if annual taxable revenue exceeds CA$30,000, corporate income tax account, and payroll deductions account if employees are hired. Instruct CRA that the entity is a Canadian unlimited liability company; if foreign-owned, evaluate the Form T2057 election for non-resident-owned ULC status for Canadian tax pass-through treatment.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Notice of Articles
Legal name and address of each director and officer
Name, date of birth, and address of authorized signatories
Estimate of first fiscal year-end and business activity description
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond in writing to any CRA request or review letter within 30 days, file a written objection under the Taxpayer Relief provisions if the BN is not activated, and correct any program account inconsistencies online in GRO (GST/HST) or via the CRA Business Window to synchronize with BC Ministry of Finance records.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business Licence and WorkSafeBC Occupational Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: City of Vancouver Business Licensing Office; WorkSafeBC (Workers' Compensation Board of British Columbia)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a Vancouver Business Licence for the registered office location and register the Corporation as an employer with WorkSafeBC. Submit the lease or occupancy permit, business activity description, and employee wage estimates. Secure the municipal fire inspection and building occupancy certification. For the social-casino software product, confirm that only virtual, non-cashable credits are used so no gaming licence under the Gaming Control Act applies; maintain records to evidence the absence of real-money wagering.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and Notice of Articles
Registered office lease or building occupancy permit
Business activity description (ISIC 5820 / NAICS 511210)
WorkSafeBC Registration application and wage estimate schedule
Fire safety and occupancy inspection certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipal licence is refused, appeal to the City of Vancouver License Inspector within 14 days or amend the business activity description to align with software publishing; for WorkSafeBC classification or assessment disputes, invoke the employer objection procedure under the Workers Compensation Act, RSBC 1996, c. 492.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: City of Vancouver Business Licensing Office (municipal operating licence); Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (federal software-publishing classification); BC Ministry of Finance – Gaming Policy and Enforcement Branch (monitoring only, as no real-money wagering is involved); WorkSafeBC (occupational safety).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: City of Vancouver Business Licence – Software Publishing (ISIC 5820 / NAICS 511210); the simulated social casino and virtual slots product does not require a licence under the Gaming Control Act, SBC 2002, c. 14, because in-game currency is non-cashable virtual credits with no redemption right.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: BC Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy – Environmental Assessment Office
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – Not triggered: the software publishing activity is office-based information technology use and does not meet any reviewable project threshold under the Environmental Assessment Act, SBC 2002, c. 43; no full EIA report, registration certificate, or environmental assessment certificate is required for this operational scope.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Office operations generate no industrial process wastewater or point-source VOC emissions. Applicable compliance thresholds: Metro Vancouver Sewer and Watercourse Protection Bylaw (prohibited waste limits; pH 6.0–10.0; no heavy metals or petroleum hydrocarbons in discharges), Vancouver Building Bylaw ventilation and indoor air quality standards for office occupancies, and disposal of electronic equipment waste under the BC Recycling Regulation, B.C. Reg. 449/2004.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: WorkSafeBC occupational health and safety registration and compliance with the Workers Compensation Act, RSBC 1996, c. 492, including injury prevention programs; municipal fire safety certification under Vancouver Fire Bylaw No. 12479 (fire suppression systems, exit signage, emergency lighting, and fire drill records); structural load inspection and occupancy permit under the Vancouver Building Bylaw; electrical safety inspection for server rooms and electronic equipment areas under the Canadian Electrical Code as adopted in BC; and workplace ergonomic and emergency-response clearance for the registered office premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — federal corporate income tax and GST/HST administration; CRA Business Registration Online (BRO) portal at canada.ca; British Columbia Ministry of Finance, Consumer Taxation Branch — British Columbia Provincial Sales Tax (PST) administration and BC eTax portal at etax.gov.bc.ca.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A BC Unlimited Liability Corporation (ULC) is deemed resident in Canada under ITA s.250(4); obtain BC incorporation certificate and articles, then apply to the CRA for a Business Number (BN) with a GST/HST program account using Form RC1 or Business Registration Online. The BN is the federal TIN; GST/HST registration is mandatory when the small-supplier threshold is exceeded. For BC PST, register separately with the BC Ministry of Finance via BC eTax using the ULC's BN and corporate details; there is no separate BC TIN. A non-resident entity carrying on business in Canada without a Canadian incorporation also files Form RC1 and may be issued a BN with applicable program accounts; for this gaming operation, Apple IAP and Google Play Billing settlement records must be tied to the BN for tax compliance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible — the BC ULC is eligible for pass-through classification under applicable foreign (e.g., U.S.) tax rules; for Canadian income tax purposes, the ULC is a taxable Canadian corporation taxed at entity level, and for foreign-owner hybrid situations the CRA may apply hybrid mismatch restrictions.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No domestic CRA 'check-the-box' election exists; the ULC is a corporation under the Income Tax Act. Available elections include ITA s.85 rollover elections for asset transfers, ITA s.93(1) foreign affiliate dividend elections, and ETA s.156 GST/HST group registration. For U.S. federal tax purposes, an IRS Form 8832 check-the-box election may elect the wholly owned BC ULC to be disregarded or treated as a partnership; Canada may then apply hybrid mismatch rules under ITA s.18.6 to deny double-deduction or deduction-without-inclusion benefits.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Federal Goods and Services Tax (GST) — a value-added tax at 5%; British Columbia Provincial Sales Tax (PST) — a retail sales tax at 7%; BC is not a Harmonized Sales Tax (HST) province.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: GST/HST: CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold measured over the immediately preceding four calendar quarters; non-resident suppliers of digital services to Canadian consumers must register for simplified GST if Canadian-source digital revenue exceeds CAD 30,000 in a 12-month period. BC PST: no small-supplier threshold; registration is triggered before the first taxable sale, lease, or licence of software/gaming services in British Columbia.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not currently impose mandatory electronic invoicing, real-time fiscal clearance, API clearance, or digital stamping. E-invoicing is optional and operates through the voluntary PEPPOL network. The CRA requires records sufficient to determine tax on taxable supplies, including invoices, app-store settlement reports, and transaction-level consumer country data; BC PST returns are filed via BC eTax and require no fiscal clearance prior to issuance of invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rated treatment applies under Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act for exported goods and for services or intangible personal property supplied to non-resident recipients where the supply is not for use or consumption in Canada. For simulated social casino and virtual slots games, the digital gaming service may be zero-rated when the user and delivery point are outside Canada and the recipient is not registered under the GST/HST. Zero-rating is denied where the Canadian market is targeted or where app-store transaction data identifies Canadian consumers. The supplier must retain credible evidence of non-resident status and foreign delivery, including App Store / Google Play storefront country, IP geolocation, payment origin, and customer contractual location. BC PST is not chargeable on software delivered outside British Columbia, but PST does not constitute an input tax credit and is not refundable through the GST/HST system.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: CBSA B13A Export Declaration (or equivalent electronic export reporting for physical goods)
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / transport documentation for exported products
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank settlement records evidencing foreign-currency consideration received
Executed master agreement, end-user licence agreement, and invoices referencing the non-resident recipient
App-store user-country, IP geolocation, and payment-origin reports proving delivery outside Canada for digital gaming services
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may scrutinize zero-rated export claims and require substantiation before refunding input tax credits or issuing export refunds. The normal reassessment period is four years, but the period is unlimited where misrepresentation or fraud is established. Penalties include civil penalties under ETA s.285.1 for false statements or omissions — $100 plus 25% of the federal tax purportedly evaded — plus statutory interest on reassessed GST/HST and clawed-back refunds. Criminal liability under ETA s.327 applies to wilful evasion. For income tax, ITA s.163(2) imposes a 50% penalty for gross-negligence false statements. BC Consumer Taxation Branch may reassess uncollected PST and impose provincial penalties where purported export delivery is not substantiated.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (monetary authority); Department of Finance Canada (foreign exchange policy lead); Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) (banking supervision); Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) (AML/EFT surveillance)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full current and capital account convertibility under IMF Article VIII; no exchange control legislation restricts capital inflows or profit remittance for non-resident owners; CAD is freely deliverable, and USD/CAD parity risk is managed through the market rather than administrative conversion quotas; ULC dividends and redemption proceeds may be repatriated without withholding deferral if subject to Canada-BC tax treaties, subject only to standard Part XIII non-resident withholding tax where applicable.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada imposes no statutory timeline, mandatory conversion ratio, or surrender obligation on export proceeds, including Apple/Google Play settlement remittances; foreign currency receipts may be held in multi-currency accounts indefinitely.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: HSBC Bank Canada (integrated into RBC since Q1 2024)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Conditional. Canadian-regulated banking status requires a Bank Act charter or Credit Union Act registration; offshore digital EMIs (Wise, Payoneer, Mercury) may serve as payment settlement facilitating accounts but do not constitute a primary licensed securities/banking relationship and, where established in Canada, must register with the Bank of Canada under the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA); social casino IAP flows routed solely through an unlicensed EMI will raise FINTRAC due diligence concerns.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Live video KYC interview is generally accepted by RBC, TD, BMO, CIBC, and Scotiabank; physical branch attendance is not statutorily mandated but is strongly encouraged for the BC-incorporated ULC, particularly because directors may be non-resident; branch presence in Vancouver is recommended for enhanced due diligence consent and for expedited USD foreign correspondent clearing approvals.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business classification as virtual slots/social casino raising potential unlicensed gambling concern under the BC Gaming Control Act and Criminal Code (Canada) sections 197 and 201
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Legal opinion from British Columbia gaming counsel confirming simulated economy only, no real-money wagering, no cash-out of virtual currency, and no 'thing of value' statutory breach; executed terms of service prohibiting secondary-market virtual chip trading; technical architecture attestation from developer; corporate compliance policy certificate; Chinese/English corporate authorization minutes.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency low-value Apple IAP / Google Play Billing payment inflows with anonymized player identities, triggering enhanced EDD under PCMLTFA/PCR
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Fully documented AML/ATF program under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA); register with FINTRAC as a Money Services Business or obtain a FINTRAC reporting-only classification where applicable; transaction monitoring rules targeting the $10,000 CAD EFT threshold; MLRO appointment and training certificates; counterparty control list evidencing Apple/Google platform verification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: ULC unlimited-liability and deemed pass-through election causing uncertainty regarding ultimate beneficial ownership and joint insolvency exposure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current BC Corporate Registry extract with 6-month updated Certificate of Good Standing; organizational certificate disclosing shareholders with >10% interest; signed ULC pass-through election or corporate-tax election documentation; registered office confirmation; resolution naming the single point of contact and Canadian-resident agent if applicable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border USD capital injections and USD profit distributions in CAD-equivalent amounts above $10,000,000 raising structured-EFP and source-of-funds red flags
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SWIFT MT103 trail with defined reference 'ULC equity contribution/inbound FDI'; audited financial statements and tax filing confirmation with CRA; bank reference letters from originating overseas institutions; shareholder statement of net worth; FATCA/CRS self-certification forms (W-8BEN-E/W-9) and signed natural person CDD file.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound equity injection via SWIFT MT103 to the BC Operational Account in CAD or USD with reference 'ULC Capital Contribution', beneficiary account at the Canadian tier-1 bank; provide FINTRAC EFT report where the injection exceeds CAD $10,000; source-of-funds dossier (investor bank statement, tax identification number, and authorized signatory resolution); route USD via the correspondent bank's New York office (CHIPS/Fedwire leg) then SWIFT conversion to CAD; no Canadian exchange-control authorization is required, but CDD documentation and FATCA/CRS self-certification are mandatory for the non-resident investor.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails: SWIFT MT103 for all international supplier payments (software development, localized storage, customer support); Apple IAP and Google Play Billing receipts arrive via mass-payment MT102/MT103 or automated B2B settlement from Apple Distribution International (Ireland) and Google APAC/EMEA entities; commercial letters of credit are not a viable or market-practice instrument for ISIC 5820 social-gaming software royalty streams; USD payouts repatriated to the Canadian operating account via bank payment gateway or SWIFT; CAD liquidity consolidated in methodology settlement account, with daily sweeps to the primary operating account.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla deliverable FX Forward (USD/CAD or EUR/CAD) with tenors of 1M-12M transacted under the bank's ISDA/CSA FX and master forward agreement
FX Swap (USD/CAD) rollover transactions for short-term settlement timing alignment
NDF (non-deliverable forward) only where the bank's FX desk verification indicates a temporarily undeliverable USD/CAD corridor, which is not the normal clearing state
Cross-currency swap (USD/CAD) for longer dated treasury structures, subject to OSFI derivative eligibility and standard initial margin posting thresholds

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: BC Annual Report (filed under s. 197 of the Business Corporations Act)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: BC Corporate Registry, Registrar of Companies (British Columbia)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due annually on the anniversary date of incorporation; the filing window opens 30 days before the anniversary date. Filings presented after the anniversary date are subject to a late fee.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late fee of approximately CAD 100 per missed filing; continued non-filing for two consecutive annual reports authorizes the Registrar to administratively dissolve the company. Assets may vest in the Crown upon dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (federal and BC provincial corporate tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due no later than 6 months after the fiscal year-end; for a December 31 year-end, the filing deadline is June 30 of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 5% of the unpaid tax balance plus 1% per month for up to 12 months under s. 162(1) of the Income Tax Act; repeated failure to file may trigger prosecution and administrative penalties.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the BC Business Corporations Act, a private ULC is exempt from mandatory annual audit; no revenue or asset thresholds require an audit. An audit becomes compulsory only if (i) the corporation is a reporting issuer under the BC Securities Act, (ii) a shareholder resolution is passed requiring an audit, or (iii) a regulator or lender contractually requires certified financial statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Private ULCs may apply Canadian ASPE or IFRS; reporting issuers must apply IFRS. Financial statements supporting the T2 return must be prepared in accordance with Canadian GAAP or IFRS, as adopted by the Accounting Standards Board.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: BC does not require a standalone annual UBO declaration to be filed. Under the BC Corporate Transparency Act, the ULC must maintain a Transparency Register and update it within 20 days of any change in significant control. As part of the annual report preparation, the directors perform an internal confirmation of the share registry and transparency register; the registers must be available to the BC Registrar on demand.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Transparency Register of Individuals with Significant Control

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 0 (not required) if completely private; USD 4,000 - 12,000 if a shareholder-approved audit is undertaken

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Combined federal and British Columbia general corporate rate: 15.0% + 12.0% = 27.0% (2024 rates, non-CCPC active income).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory tax holiday. Available reductions/credits: federal SR&ED investment tax credit at 15% non-refundable generally or 35% refundable for qualifying Canadian-controlled private corporations (CCPCs) within expenditure limits; British Columbia refundable R&D tax credit at 10% of eligible SR&ED expenditures. For qualifying CCPCs, the small business deduction reduces federal tax to 9.0% and BC tax to 2.0%, producing an 11.0% combined rate on active business income up to CAD 500,000.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (combined federal and BC provincial corporate tax return due to the Canada-British Columbia Tax Collection Agreement), filed electronically via CRA E-file through authorized third-party software or EFILE; provincially administered through the same T2 return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual T2 return for each taxation year; quarterly or monthly instalments of estimated Part I and BC income tax may be required under CRA instalment thresholds.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing deadline is six months after the corporation's taxation year-end (e.g., a December 31 year-end requires filing by June 30). Tax instalments are due approximately four, six, nine, and twelve months into the taxation year in prescribed circumstances.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, business number, registered office address, jurisdiction of incorporation, year-end, mailing address, and fiscal period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident-controlled BC unlimited liability corporation (ULC) must provide the Canadian agent or representative contact and disclose beneficial foreign shareholders on Schedule 91; ensure Canada Revenue Agency has an up-to-date authorized representative on file.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Assets, liabilities, share capital, retained earnings/contributed surplus, and equity as at taxation year-end, prepared in Canadian dollars.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report IFRS or acceptable accounting figures converted to CAD at the Bank of Canada annual average exchange rate; disclose all intercompany receivable/payable balances with the US parent or finance entities to support transfer-pricing analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue, cost of sales, operating expenses, net income before adjustments, and extraordinary items for the taxation period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: When the Canadian ULC is the principal operating entity, recognize mobile in-app purchase revenue on a gross basis and deduct Apple IAP and Google Play Billing commissions as operating expenses; do not net these commissions off revenue unless the corporation is a pass-through agent under IFRS 15, which is unlikely for an active publisher.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Schedule 1 – Net Income to Taxable Income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation of accounting net income to taxable income, including non-deductible expenses, deductible reserves, capital gains/allowable capital losses, and timing adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For illicit transfer pricing or excessive royalties, adjust taxable income under section 247; add back any management fees paid to foreign affiliates that lack arm's length support. Also include foreign accrual property income (FAPI) adjustments under section 91 if the ULC holds passive interests in foreign affiliates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 950 – Total Tax Payable and Credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculation of Part I federal tax, BC provincial tax, dividend refund, tax credits, instalments paid, and balance due or refund receivable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the corporation is a branch of a non-resident parent for domestic law purposes, support the allocation of BC tax and branch loss carryback by attached financial statements and a fully prepared Schedule 91; a foreign parent does not reduce Canadian-source income except through valid transfer pricing and treaty provisions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late-filing penalty under ITA section 162(1)/162(2): 5% of unpaid Part I tax plus 1% per full month late, to a maximum of 12 months; repeat failure within three years: 10% plus 2% per month, to a maximum 24 months. CRA also charges interest at prescribed rates on unpaid taxes and instalments. Late or inaccurate filings can trigger gross-negligence penalties of 50% of understated tax under section 163(2) and provincial penalties under the Income Tax Act, R.S.B.C. 1996, c. 166.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% Part XIII withholding tax under ITA section 212(2) on dividends paid by a Canadian-resident corporation to a non-resident shareholder. Under the Canada-US Tax Treaty, reduced to 5% where the U.S. payee is a company that owns at least 10% of the voting stock of the Canadian payer, otherwise 15%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke treaty relief, the non-resident shareholder must be the beneficial owner and must provide a valid certificate of residency from the home-country tax authority before or at the time of payment. For U.S. payees, provide a U.S. Certificate of Residency or IRS Form 6166. The Canadian payer retains this certificate in its contemporaneous files and may reduce the withholding rate at source. CRA forms NR301/NR302 may be presented by the payee where CRA so requires; if excess tax is withheld, the non-resident can file a treaty-based refund claim with CRA within the applicable limitation period, attaching the certificate and an explanation of the relevant article.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates under Part XIII: 25% on interest paid to non-residents and 25% on royalties for use of or the right to use any intellectual property. Under the Canada-US Tax Treaty, arm's length interest is generally exempt from Canadian withholding tax (Article XI), and qualifying royalties are generally exempt (Article XII), subject to treaty-specific exceptions, including contingent interest potentially taxed at 15% and certain copyright royalties related to Canadian cultural entitlement. For non-treaty countries the statutory 25% rate applies.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Canada imposes a contemporaneous documentation expectation where the aggregate value of covered cross-border non-arm's length transactions in a taxation year exceeds CAD 1 million; CRA administrative practice also considers gross revenue of CAD 10 million as part of a materiality test. For country-by-country reporting, an ultimate parent or surrogate parent must file CbC Report when the MNE group's consolidated revenue is at least CAD 750 million. Documentation must include a Master File and a Local File when requested; the Local File must identify the tested parties and apply a comparability analysis.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not have standalone Economic Substance Regulations comparable to those in the UAE or other offshore finance centres. However, Canadian jurisprudence applying the general anti-avoidance rule (GAAR) under ITA section 245 and the doctrine of sham requires every taxpayer to show economic reality, business purpose, and genuine operational substance. For a BC ULC, tax authorities will examine whether the corporation has Canadian offices, employees, board activity, decision-making, books, records, and actual risk-taking; a ULC lacking such substance may be disregarded or the transactions recharacterized for Canadian tax purposes.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willfully underreporting social-casino in-app purchase revenue, manufacturing fake Apple IAP or Google Play Billing commission invoices, intentionally omitting foreign-source revenue, or using fraudulent charitable or affiliate structures to conceal taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil gross-negligence penalty under ITA section 163(2) in the amount of 50% of the federal tax understated; provincial penalty on the BC income tax understated. Criminal prosecution under section 239 of the Income Tax Act: fine of 50% to 200% of the tax sought to be evaded, up to five years imprisonment on indictment, restitution orders, and court-ordered asset forfeiture.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who authorize false filings may be jointly and severally liable for unremitted source deductions and GST/HST under section 227.1; CRA can seize personal bank accounts, garnish wages, and pursue travel bans or criminal convictions that bar cross-border movement. Directors may also be personally liable to the Crown for civil fraud under common law piercing of the corporate veil.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Corporation / GAAR Abuse / Unrealistic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a BC unlimited liability corporation as a nominee shell for a U.S. parent, with no employees in Canada, no real game development or publishing activity, and a contrived structure that strips all Canadian profits through deductible royalties, management fees, interest, or dividends without economic substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR permits CRA to deny the tax benefit and reassess; transfer-pricing penalty under section 247(3) may impose a 10% penalty on understated taxable income; treaty benefits may be denied under Canada-US Treaty Limitation on Benefits provisions; BC registrar may dissolve the corporation for failure to meet annual filing requirements under the BC Business Corporations Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: In a ULC, shareholders bear unlimited liability for corporate obligations, and directors can be personally liable for knowing participation in fraudulent preferences, illegal dividends, or misrepresentations in corporate filings. Court-ordered restitution may extend to personal assets, and directors may face travel bans in connection with civil fraud proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Money Laundering / Unlicensed Real-Money Gaming
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a social-casino product that permits secondary markets in virtual chips, cash-out conversion, swap transactions, or unlicensed real-money wagers while failing to register as a money services business under FINTRAC, failing to implement know-your-client and suspicious transaction reporting, or moving IAP proceeds through opaque digital wallet or shell accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative monetary penalties under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act of up to CAD 1 million per violation for entities and up to CAD 500,000 for individuals; criminal money laundering under Criminal Code section 462.31 punishable by up to 10 years imprisonment; unlicensed casino-related gaming in British Columbia is also an offence under the Gaming Control Act, exposing the corporation to fines and forfeiture of proceeds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers can be criminally liable where they direct or participate in money laundering or knowingly benefit from the proceeds. Under Bill C-45 provisions on criminal liability of organizations, senior officers may be personally convicted if they knew or were criminally negligent. Civil restitution to victims of unlicensed gaming and asset freezes may also be ordered, with director travel restrictions imposed pending extradition or fraud investigations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Part XIII / NR4 Withholding Violations on Non-Resident Distributions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, royalties, or interest to a non-resident controlling shareholder without deducting the required 25% Part XIII withholding tax, or without a properly documented treaty exemption; misclassifying dividend or royalty payments as service fees to avoid withholding; failing to file NR4 returns or failing to disclose non-resident beneficial ownership to CRA.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under ITA section 227(8), interest accrues on unremitted withheld amounts; section 227(9) imposes a penalty of 10% of the amount that should have been withheld. CRA may assess the payer for the entire unreported Part XIII tax amount under section 227(4), with no corresponding deduction in the payer's income; failure to file NR4 returns attracts penalties of CAD 25 per day per return, up to CAD 2,500 per return, plus late-filing penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Section 227.1 imposes joint and several personal liability on directors for unremitted withholding tax if they failed to exercise reasonable diligence. In cross-border structures, the Canadian agent or resident representative of a non-resident ULC can also be personally liable for unreported Part XIII tax. Directors may face civil suits for restitution, seizure of personal assets, and in egregious cases travel bans while CRA and the Public Prosecution Service pursue criminal sanctions.
